page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with a dedicated 32-core AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at 2.55 GHz, providing 64 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The system includes 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The CPU features 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, with instruction set support including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA. This instance features no local disk storage or attached GPUs and includes 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.c7a.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-threaded performance, recording a multi-core stress-ng score of 86349.63 and a PassMark CPU score of 59199.92. Memory performance shows strong throughput for cached small-block transfers at 4132.73 GB/sec, alongside a PassMark memory score of 2970.96. Specialized workloads show strong execution in Redis SET operations at 61.81 million operations per second, PassMark database operations, and small 135M parameter LLM inference. However, uncached large-block memory read at 85.04 GB/sec and write at 38.03 GB/sec fall into average ranges, and the CPU lacks AVX-512 extensions.

The instance provides high compute density for workloads that do not require high memory capacity per core or local NVMe storage. Omitting bundled local disk capacity allows cost efficiency focused strictly on vCPU allocation when attached network storage is utilized. Given its high core count, cryptography extensions, and strong database benchmark results, the ecs.c7a.16xlarge is suited for multi-threaded software compilation, in-memory key-value stores, batch data processing, high-concurrency web serving, and lightweight model inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a dedicated 32-core AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and instruction set support for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, while lacking local storage and GPUs. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-core processing, high cached memory bandwidth, and performant Redis SET and database operations, though uncached large-block memory transfers and single-core metrics sit at average performance tiers. The configuration offers efficient resource allocation for compute-intensive tasks without unused memory overhead. The instance is suited for high-concurrency database workloads, parallelized software compilation, batch processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
